tagline: From the Seto Inland Sea to the Yaeyama Islands — a nation of 14,000 islands.
summary: Japan is an archipelago of roughly 14,000 islands, its coasts and inland sea threaded by centuries of maritime culture. The Seto Inland Sea — with the art islands of Naoshima and Teshima and the bridge-linked Shimanami chain — and the subtropical Yaeyama and Okinawa islands are among its most distinctive destinations, reached today by conventional ferries. A clean, stabilised foiling tier is the premium layer between the local ferry and the absent on-demand option.
why_marine_mobility: No single city brief tells the Japanese coastal story, because it IS the Seto Inland Sea and the southern island chains. The Setouchi art islands draw a global cultural-tourism audience onto slow local ferries; the Yaeyama group around Ishigaki depends on inter-island boats for daily life and tourism. Navier's Pioneer II foiling tier turns these ferry hops into smooth, dry, on-demand crossings, while the Quanta-LR hybrid range opens long coastal trunks — such as the Setouchi-to-Tokyo Bay run — that no day-boat can serve.

demand_signals.label: Setouchi cultural-tourism volume
demand_signals.note: The Seto Inland Sea art islands (Naoshima, Teshima, and the Setouchi Triennale) draw a large international audience that moves entirely by inter-island ferry.

demand_signals.label: Inter-island necessity
demand_signals.note: The Yaeyama and Okinawa island groups depend on ferry links for daily transport, healthcare access and tourism — core infrastructure, not discretionary travel.

demand_signals.label: Premium-travel maturity
demand_signals.note: Japan's inbound luxury and experiential travel market is large and growing; a clean, premium water tier fits an audience already paying for high-end rail and ryokan experiences.

demand_signals.label: Aging-region resilience
demand_signals.note: Many inland-sea and southern islands have aging populations for whom reliable, comfortable, weather-resilient marine links are an essential-service question.

use_cases.body: Ishigaki to Kabira Bay and the Yaeyama gateway: a subtropical inter-island hop today run on local ferries — ideal for a smooth, dry, premium foiling tier.
Setouchi art-island hopping: clean, quiet foiling shuttles between Naoshima, Teshima and the Inland Sea ports, matching the refined character of the destination.
Seto Inland Sea to Tokyo Bay: a long-range Quanta-LR coastal trunk linking the Inland Sea cultural corridor to the capital — a crossing no battery day-boat can serve.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The inter-island hops — the Yaeyama group around Ishigaki (~18–20 nm) and the Seto Inland Sea art-island links — sit comfortably inside Pioneer II's 70-nautical-mile range at 30 knots, commercial-ready today.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The long coastal trunk from the Seto Inland Sea toward Tokyo Bay (~320 nm) is Quanta-LR territory (~700 nm hybrid range, H2 2026+), opening corridors no day-boat can reach.

signature_routes.label: Seto Inland Sea ↔ Tokyo Bay — the long-range coastal trunk
Ishigaki (Yaeyama gateway) ↔ Kabira Bay — the subtropical island hop

transit_planning: For a tourism authority or a regional operator: a clean, quiet, low-emission water tier that matches the refined character of the Setouchi art islands and brings weather-resilient comfort to the southern island chains. Start with the proven Yaeyama and Inland Sea hops on Pioneer II, then add the long Setouchi–Tokyo Bay coastal trunk on Quanta-LR as range comes online.
competitive_landscape: Island travel today runs almost entirely on conventional local ferries — reliable and affordable, but slow, fixed-schedule and unremarkable. There is effectively no on-demand premium tier. Navier's foiling craft is the missing premium-but-practical option: faster, smoother and quieter than a local ferry, cleaner than diesel craft, and matched to a high-end travel market that has no comparable water product today.
regulatory_note: Japanese domestic maritime transport is regulated by the Maritime Bureau of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) and the Japan Coast Guard; passenger operation requires vessel certification and route licensing. Okinawa Prefecture and the Setouchi regional authorities are natural first touchpoints.
seasonality: The Seto Inland Sea is sheltered and navigable year-round, with peak cultural-tourism demand around the Setouchi Triennale seasons; the subtropical Yaeyama group is busiest outside the summer typhoon window (peak risk Aug–Sep). A stabilised foiling craft holds comfort and schedule across choppy shoulder-season conditions.

precedents.what: Four Seasons Lake Austin operates an N30 in live luxury-hospitality service — proof of the premium water-shuttle model Navier brings to Japan's island corridors.
